steps.label: Steps
steps.sideNote: All data in this demonstration is illustrative. This is not a production tool.

metric.label: Indicator
metric.ptLong: Plant share of protein sold (Protein Tracker)
metric.fg1Long: Plant share of protein-rich foods, in tonnes of product (WWF FG1)

baseline.title: Starting point
baseline.desc: The reference protein ratio, broken down over your 4 plots and the rest of the protein sold.
baseline.keyMessageText: Most of the plant protein sold comes from pasta, bread and cereals. The 4 plots are where action happens, not yet where the volume is.
baseline.keyMessageFg1: In WWF FG1, only {plot1} and {plot3} count: {plot2} are mixed products, set apart, and {plot4} belong to group FG2.
baseline.plantNotePt: In ratio points and tonnes of protein
baseline.plantNoteFg1: In ratio points and tonnes of product, protein-rich foods (FG1)
baseline.animalNoteFg1: Share of protein-rich foods, in tonnes of product

levers.title: Levers
levers.desc: Twenty levers, each quantified from explicit assumptions. Click a lever to open its sheet and change its assumptions.
levers.isolatedNote: Each lever alone, with your assumptions and {adoption} of stores following.
levers.matrixNote: Indicative scores from the deck, 0 to 10. The positions of levers 8 and 10 are provisional.

trajectory.title: Trajectory
trajectory.desc: Switch levers on, set the share of stores that follow, and read the effect by lever or over time.
trajectory.adoptionNote: In a cooperative network, the central office recommends and each store decides. This slider sets the share of stores that apply the levers concerned.
trajectory.adoptionNoEffect: No effect here: the active levers are all decided centrally.
trajectory.overlapNote: Levers partly touch the same products: their effects do not add up.
trajectory.stackNotePt: In ratio points: the total height is the ratio
trajectory.chartTitleLever: From the {from} reference to {to}, lever by lever
trajectory.noLever: No active lever. Choose a scenario or tick some levers.
trajectory.extensionNote: Beyond {year}: diffusion assumption, lever effects grow by {rate} a year.
trajectory.dutchSource: Pace observed in the Netherlands: {text} Source: {source}.

data.title: With your data
data.desc: What the demonstration cannot show without your real data, and what that data would make possible.
data.storesWith: customer profiles and catchment areas for each store
data.storesGet: the stores where pilots should start, and adoption estimated store by store
data.marginGet: a quantified trade-off between margin and ratio, lever by lever
data.carbonWith: emission factors for your products and suppliers
data.carbonGet: CO2 calibrated on your range, instead of an order of magnitude
data.salesWith: weekly sales of pilot stores and control stores
data.salesGet: pilot tracking, and roll-out decisions based on measured figures
data.historyWith: several years of sales, prices and promotions
data.historyGet: elasticities estimated on your shoppers, instead of default assumptions
data.note: Each module is built on your data, within a framework agreed together.

drawer.title: Lever sheet
drawer.effectNote: Lever alone, with these assumptions and {adoption} of stores following
drawer.storeShare: Store dependency {dep}: with {adoption} of stores following, {factor} of the full effect.
drawer.noRatioEffect: Does not move the ratio, makes the measurement more reliable.
drawer.tightening: Gap between low and high bounds of every other lever multiplied by {k}.
drawer.footer: Each assumption is a question to check with the team concerned.

tour.s1Text: The 2025 reference protein ratio: the plant share of protein sold. Illustrative data.
tour.s2Text: The 4 plots weigh a few points: most plant protein comes from pasta, bread and cereals.
tour.s3Text: Each lever is quantified by explicit assumptions. Click a lever to change them.
tour.s4Text: The central office recommends, stores decide: this slider sets the share that applies the levers.
tour.s5Text: The waterfall shows what each lever brings, the curve shows the pace year by year.
